subsystems.name: Telescope and optics
subsystems.role: collects starlight with enough precision to track the host star during transit.

subsystems.name: Spectrograph
subsystems.role: splits the light into wavelengths so absorption features can be measured.

subsystems.name: Data acquisition and control
subsystems.role: records spectra at high cadence and keeps the instrument stable.

subsystems.name: Stellar and planetary models
subsystems.role: predicts the star's spectrum and the transit geometry to isolate the planet's signal.

subsystems.name: Analysis pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw spectra into a transmission spectrum and fits atmospheric models.

buildSteps.title: Select a target
buildSteps.detail: Choose a transiting exoplanet with a bright host star and a known orbit, preferably a hot Jupiter or a small planet around a small star.

buildSteps.title: Plan the observation
buildSteps.detail: Schedule telescope time to cover the full transit plus out-of-transit baseline, often several hours.

buildSteps.title: Collect spectra
buildSteps.detail: Point the telescope at the star and take repeated spectra at a cadence of seconds to minutes before, during, and after transit.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the data
buildSteps.detail: Correct for detector artifacts, cosmic rays, and instrument systematics using calibration frames and reference stars.

buildSteps.title: Extract the transmission spectrum
buildSteps.detail: Measure the wavelength-dependent dip in starlight during transit and subtract the out-of-transit spectrum to isolate the planet's absorption.

buildSteps.title: Model the atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Fit the transmission spectrum with atmospheric models to infer molecules, temperature, and clouds.

buildSteps.title: Validate and publish
buildSteps.detail: Check for stellar contamination and systematic errors, then report the detection and its significance.

prerequisites.why: Earth's atmosphere absorbs key molecules like water and carbon dioxide, so space is needed for a clean spectrum.
the transit signal is a tiny fraction of the star's light, requiring very stable and sensitive instruments.
they translate absorption features into physical properties like composition and temperature.
starspots and faculae can mimic or hide planetary signals and are not always well modelled.
rocky planets around Sun-like stars give signals too faint for current telescopes except a few favourable cases.

pathway.milestone: JWST and Hubble detect molecules in the atmospheres of hot Jupiters and some smaller planets.
pathway.unlocks: a first inventory of exoplanet compositions and a check for hydrogen envelopes.

pathway.milestone: Dedicated survey missions such as ESA's Ariel study a large sample of planets.
pathway.unlocks: statistical understanding of how atmospheres vary with planet type and star.

pathway.milestone: Ground-based extremely large telescopes use high-resolution spectroscopy to probe biosignatures.
pathway.unlocks: the ability to search for oxygen, methane, and other potential signs of life.

pathway.milestone: Direct imaging spectroscopy of Earth-like planets around Sun-like stars.
pathway.unlocks: characterisation of truly habitable worlds without the need for a transit.
